parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Calculate the number of people in Guinea that are under the age of 25.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest reasons why 60% of the population in Guinea is under the age of 25.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Suggest two impacts of a youthful age structure on a less economically developed
country (LEDC).

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
The photograph shows a young person transporting goods in Guinea.
Describe three pieces of evidence in the photograph that suggest Guinea is a less
economically developed country (LEDC).

Peanuts are an important cash crop grown by many farmers in Guinea.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
The green leaves of the peanut plants are used in the process of photosynthesis.
Describe the process of photosynthesis.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The flowers of peanut plants are self-pollinating. This means that insects do not have to
visit every flower for pollination to occur.
Describe the process of pollination in peanut flowers.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Oil is extracted from peanuts.
The peanut oil is exported to many countries.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one benefit of exporting peanut oil instead of peanuts.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest two possible uses for the peanut waste after the peanut oil has been extracted.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Suggest reasons why the government of Guinea encourages farmers to grow peanuts.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The farmers use the same fields to grow peanuts each year.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest why the farmers expect the yield of peanuts to go down after several years.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The stems and leaves of the peanut plants can be used to feed livestock.
Suggest how this helps make peanut farming a sustainable activity.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Some peanut farmers are not able to keep livestock.
Suggest other ways these farmers can make their farming sustainable.

text: A student talks to a peanut farmer.
I have two fields of peanuts, field A and field B. I usually harvest more peanuts
from field A. I think the harvest from field B is being reduced by insect pests on
the leaves and on the soil.
The student decides to investigate how many insect pests there are in each field.

parts.text:
Phosphate is a mineral ion that is present in a fertile soil.
State the names of two other mineral ions that are present in a fertile soil.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Mineral ions are a component of soil.
State three other components of soil.

The farmer uses bunds in field A and field B to reduce soil erosion.
State one other strategy for reducing soil erosion.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
The compressed earth building blocks have holes in them to make them hollow.
Suggest two benefits of making the building blocks hollow.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The compressed earth building blocks can also be made by hand.
Suggest two advantages of making the building blocks by machine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Hollow building blocks are also made from cement.
The process of making cement releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Explain how releasing carbon dioxide into the atmosphere contributes to the enhanced
greenhouse effect.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
State the name of one gas, other than carbon dioxide, that contributes to the enhanced
greenhouse effect.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Wood can also be used for building.
An advantage of using wood for building is that it limits the use of cement.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest two other ways the government of Guinea can limit the use of cement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest two disadvantages of using wood for building.

4 Mining is an important industry in Guinea.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: The photograph shows an open-pit diamond mine in Guinea.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest reasons why there is less risk of injury and death working in an open-pit mine
compared with working in a shaft mine.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest reasons why local people want diamond mining to continue in the area.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Explain why an environmental impact assessment must be completed before a mining
licence can be issued.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Describe ways the landscape shown in the photograph can be restored after all the
mining is finished.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
There is a large global demand for rocks and minerals.
Describe strategies for the sustainable use of rocks and minerals.
